question.text: If the straight line drawn through the point <math> <mrow> <mtext>P</mtext> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <msqrt> <mn>3</mn> </msqrt> <mtext>, </mtext> <mn>2</mn></mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </math> and inclined at an angle <math> <mrow> <mfrac> <mrow> <mi>π</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>6</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </math> with the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> - axis meets the line <math> <mrow><msqrt> <mn>3</mn> </msqrt> <mtext>x</mtext><mo>-</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mtext>y</mtext> <mo>+</mo> <mn>8</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </mrow> </math> at <math> <mrow> <mtext>Q,</mtext></mrow> </math> then the length of <math> <mrow> <mtext>PQ</mtext></mrow> </math> is

solution.text:
Point Q can be obtained by using parametric form of a straight line, ⇒Q≡3-3r2,  2-r2 

Also, point Q is on 3 x - 4 y + 8   so it will satisfy this equation, hence, 

33-3r2-4 2-r2+8=0

3 - 3 2 r - 8 + 2 r + 8 = 0

⇒r2-32=-3 ⇒r=-6

Hence, the length of PQ=6
